root_cause.text: The sbi->sync_decompress field is accessed after queue_work() is called, creating a race condition where the filesystem can be unmounted and sbi freed before the queued work accesses this field.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the sbi->sync_decompress modification from after queue_work() (lines 1474-1476 in the original code) to before queue_work() (lines 1458-1460 in the patched code). The CVE description shows that z_erofs_decompressqueue_work() can execute after all folios are unlocked, allowing the unmount thread to proceed and free sbi via erofs_sb_free() before the decompression work accesses sbi->sync_decompress. By moving the sbi modification before queue_work(), the access occurs while sbi is still guaranteed to be valid, eliminating the use-after-free window.

intent_record.intent_summary: Force synchronous decompression mode when in atomic context to prevent scheduling violations or deadlocks from attempting asynchronous decompression.
intent_record.what: Added three lines within the `z_erofs_in_atomic()` conditional block: a comment referencing sysfs documentation and two lines that conditionally update `sbi->sync_decompress` from `EROFS_SYNC_DECOMPRESS_AUTO` to `EROFS_SYNC_DECOMPRESS_FORCE_ON` when in atomic context.
intent_record.how: When the decompression queue is in atomic context (detected by `z_erofs_in_atomic()`), the code now automatically transitions the sync_decompress mode from AUTO to FORCE_ON. This forces synchronous decompression behavior when atomic constraints prevent asynchronous decompression, preventing potential deadlocks or scheduling violations that could occur if decompression were attempted asynchronously in atomic context.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove automatic sync_decompress mode promotion logic that was incorrectly transitioning decompression behavior during runtime.
intent_record.what: Removed three lines of code that conditionally set `sbi->sync_decompress` to `EROFS_SYNC_DECOMPRESS_FORCE_ON` when it was previously set to `EROFS_SYNC_DECOMPRESS_AUTO`, along with its explanatory comment referencing sysfs-fs-erofs documentation.
intent_record.how: This change eliminates the automatic state transition logic that would force synchronous decompression mode on after the first asynchronous decompression work is queued. After this removal, the sync_decompress setting will no longer be automatically promoted from AUTO to FORCE_ON during decompression kickoff, allowing it to remain in its initial state or be controlled only through explicit configuration.

In the `z_erofs_decompress_kickoff()` function (lines 1473-1476), after `queue_work(z_erofs_workqueue, &io->u.work)` is executed at line 1472, the code immediately accesses `sbi->sync_decompress` at line 1474-1475 to modify it.     erofs: fix use-after-free of on-stack io[]
    
    The root cause is the race as follows:
    Thread #1                              Thread #2(irq ctx)
    
    z_erofs_runqueue()
      struct z_erofs_decompressqueue io_A[];

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit FIXES the vulnerability rather than introducing it. The vulnerable construct was the use of `wake_up_locked(&io->u.wait)` on a stack-allocated `io[]` array after `queue_work()` could allow the work to execute and access the wait queue after the stack frame is destroyed. The fix replaces the waitqueue mechanism with `complete(&io->u.done)` and changes the wait from `io_wait_event(io[JQ_SUBMIT].u.wait, ...)` to `wait_for_completion_io(&io[JQ_SUBMIT].u.done)`. This eliminates the race condition because completion objects are properly synchronized and don't have the same use-after-free vulnerability as stack-based waitqueues. The vulnerable construct (wake_up_locked on stack-allocated io[]) is REMOVED in this commit, making it a fix commit, not a bug-introducing commit.
